root_cause.text: Array bounds checking used `>` instead of `>=` comparison operators, allowing out-of-bounds array access when indices equal the maximum valid index in the rockchip rkcif MIPI capture driver.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes comparisons from `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE` to `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)` and similar changes for `index` and `id` parameters. Since array indices are zero-based, a valid index range for an array of size N is [0, N-1], making `>=` the correct comparison operator. The original `>` comparison would allow index value equal to the array size to pass validation, resulting in out-of-bounds access when used to index the arrays in subsequent operations.

intent_record.what: Replaced two hardcoded boundary checks (block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE and index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX) with dynamic array size checks using ARRAY_SIZE() macro on the actual data structures (rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks and rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs). Changed comparison operators from > to >= to match array bounds semantics.
intent_record.how: This change makes the bounds checking dynamic and data-driven rather than relying on hardcoded constants. The ARRAY_SIZE() macro computes the actual size of the arrays at compile time, ensuring the checks always match the true array dimensions. Using >= instead of > correctly prevents out-of-bounds access (valid indices are 0 to size-1). This eliminates the risk of hardcoded constants becoming stale if the underlying data structures change.

Author: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@collabora.com>

    media: rockchip: rkcif: add support for rk3568 vicap mipi capture
    
    The RK3568 Video Capture (VICAP) unit features a MIPI CSI-2 capture
    interface. Add support for the MIPI capture interface in general
    and for the RK3568 VICAP MIPI capture in particular.
    
    Signed-off-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@wolfvision.net>
    Reviewed-b
bic_trace_step.reason: The function contains the vulnerable construct at line 492-493. The bounds checking uses `>` (greater than) instead of `>=` (greater than or equal to) operators. Specifically: (1) Line 492 checks `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`, which allows `block` to equal `RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`, potentially causing out-of-bounds access to `rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks[block]` at line 496 when the index equals the maximum valid index. (2) Line 493 checks `index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX`, which allows `index` to equal `RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX`, potentially causing out-of-bounds access to `rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs[index]` at line 497. The correct checks should use `>=` to reject indices that equal or exceed the maximum bounds, not just those strictly greater than the bounds.
